# Vendored: compiled Tailwind CSS (not the Play CDN)

`tailwind.css` is a static build generated by the real Tailwind CLI
(`tailwindcss`, pinned in `../../package.json`) from the utility classes
actually used in `index.html`/`app.js`/`js/**/*.js` (see
`../../tailwind.config.js`'s `content` globs), committed here instead of
loaded from `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com`.

This is the same fix already applied to `dapjs` (see `../dapjs/README.md`)
for the same reason: a real reported bug traced back to a CDN script that
has to fetch *and execute* before anything works. The Play CDN variant is
worse than a plain unpinned script -- it's JavaScript that scans the
whole DOM at runtime to generate CSS on the fly, which Tailwind's own
docs say outright not to use in production. On a slow or filtered school
network it can silently never finish, and every element depending on it
-- icons above all, since an `<svg>` with no intrinsic size falls back to
the browser's bare default -- renders broken instead. Students on exactly
that kind of network reported seeing giant, unstyled icons and nothing
else; switching to a plain `<link rel="stylesheet">` to a file that's
already on disk means the page looks right regardless of what the
network does afterward.

**To rebuild** (after adding/removing/changing any Tailwind utility class
anywhere in the scanned files):

```bash
cd frontend
npm install   # once, or whenever package.json changes
npm run build:css
```

This is the one thing the CDN used to do automatically that a static
build doesn't: a brand-new class typed into the HTML/JS does nothing
until this command re-runs. If something looks unstyled after an edit,
rebuild before assuming it's a real bug.
